anticipatory.title: Iran deal versus Saudi restraint
parts: What Is Priced

Brent closed at 92.97 USD/bbl, -1.94% on the session but +5.19% over 20, with WTI at 91.76 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), as Reuters reported the US in the very final stages of Iran nuclear talks [[n1501]]. The market is pricing some deal probability without pricing new barrels soon.
Conditional Expression

A signed deal would pressure crude and lift refiners and airlines; Reuters reported Asian refiners eager to resume Iranian oil imports as high prices bite [[n2011]]. No deal plus escalation in Ukraine fits the case Bloomberg made that oil's Covid crash set the world up for $100 crude [[n0142]]; then add XLE and USO.
Risk

Saudi restraint limits any offset: The Intercept reported Saudi Arabia rejecting Biden's plea to increase oil production as midterms loom [[n1971]]. The draft's oil-later sequencing, which Reuters detailed [[n1514]], makes a deal less bearish for crude than headlines imply, so short-crude expressions need a signed text, not optimism.

catalysts.title: Walmart (WMT): grocery share gains as the inflation hedge
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Walmart is converting inflation into sales. Al Jazeera reported it thriving despite supply-chain woes and high inflation [[n0972]], and Reuters reported its Mexico unit lifting profit 5% even as costs increased [[n1211]]. Scale lets Walmart hold price gaps that smaller grocers cannot, and grocery share is the stickiest form of revenue.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock rose 4.01% to 138.88 USD but remains below its 20-session-earlier 141.22 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: CNBC reported shoppers on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0974]], and trade-down could squeeze mix.
Trade Expression
Buy on a close above 141.22 USD, paired against Target, -7.99% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), to isolate scale. Cut if the stock gives back its results-day gain.

catalysts.title: Cisco (CSCO): beat, raise and buy back
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported Cisco raising its annual earnings forecast and announcing $15 bln in share buybacks [[n1184]], and CNBC's Investing Club described it as defying the doubters [[n1196]]; the buyback adds a dependable bid. WSJ reported a $20 billion-plus takeover offer for Splunk [[n1097]], showing management will use the balance sheet to buy recurring software revenue. Hardware with visible orders is the rewarded profile on this tape.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Cisco rose 2.80% to 55.77 USD but is -3.98% over 20 sessions against a 20-session-earlier 58.08 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: a large acquisition at a premium would dilute buyback capacity.
Trade Expression
Accumulate below 58.08 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) and add on a close above it. Reassess if a Splunk deal comes with a premium that crowds out repurchases.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA): upbeat guide, sold anyway
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Nvidia announced fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0141]] and, per Al Jazeera, forecast upbeat current-quarter revenue [[n1987]]. The franchise is intact; the problem is a valuation that already discounted the beat, in a tape that punishes duration. Competition is rising too, after Reuters reported AMD closing its estimated $50 billion Xilinx purchase [[n0445]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock fell 7.56% to 245.07 USD, close to its 20-session-earlier 241.50 USD and still +1.48% over that span (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: AMD's 4.52% fall the same day shows the whole complex de-rating together.
Trade Expression
Wait: buy only on a hold above 241.50 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) with the SOX stabilising. A close below that level would erase its 20-session gain and argue for patience.

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC): the comeback plan needs proof
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Bloomberg reported Intel's CEO tired of Wall Street doubting his comeback plan [[n1195]], and The New York Times asked whether Intel can make a comeback as the world needs what it makes [[n0960]]. Tom's Hardware reported AMD's market cap surpassing Intel's for the first time in history [[n0540]], the scoreboard investors are watching. Intel's agreed $5.4 billion purchase of Tower Semiconductor [[n0612]] adds foundry capacity to the plan.
Price Hurdle & Risk
Intel fell 1.37% to 47.57 USD and is -8.59% over 20 sessions from 52.04 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk: heavy capex delays free cash flow for years.
Trade Expression
Hold a starter position; add on a close above 52.04 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Cut if foundry milestones slip.

catalysts.title: Palantir (PLTR): commercial push, margin pain
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported that Palantir's margins will take a hit from higher spending in its commercial push [[n0941]]. In a market paying for near-term cash, management chose growth spending over margin, and investors repriced the stock immediately. Peers confirm the pattern: C3.ai fell 9.55% and Snowflake 6.05% on the same session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
Price Hurdle & Risk

Palantir fell 15.75% to 11.77 USD and is -19.49% over 20 sessions from 14.62 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Risk to the bearish view: a short-covering bounce in a stock this heavily sold.
Trade Expression
Stay underweight; reassess only on a close back above 14.62 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17) or evidence that commercial wins are lifting operating leverage.

catalysts.title: Deere (DE): farm pricing versus freight costs
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Barron's previewed Deere's earnings, which it said are coming Friday [[n0150]]. Strong crop prices support farm incomes, with soybeans +11.66% and corn +6.38% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), and the open question is whether Deere's pricing outruns steel, freight and labour costs.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Deere fell 2.57% to 380.53 USD but is +3.69% over 20 sessions from 366.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), outperforming Caterpillar's -10.10%. Risk: a margin miss would follow the market's pattern of punishing spending, whatever the order book shows.
Trade Expression
Wait for the print. Buy a close above 380.53 USD on confirmed price realisation; avoid below 366.98 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), where the 20-session outperformance would be gone.

spec.retail_intro: Friday's crowd story is conviction under fire: Palantir's margin warning [[n0941]] landed on the day war fear returned and just after Charlie Munger said retail trading apps are creating a speculative mess [[n1869]], the moment when a belief-driven shareholder base either buys the dip or starts to bleed.

retail.title: Palantir Technologies / PLTR — the growth bill hits the faithful
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Palantir is a stock its holders own as a belief system: a data-software company they expect to grow from government work into big commercial customers, run by a chief executive whose mystique is part of the appeal, down to the sponsored Norwegian ski clothes NRKbeta wrote up as a mystery [[n0669]]. On Thursday the faithful got the bill for that commercial push: Reuters reports Palantir margins will take a hit from higher spending [[n0941]], and the stock fell 15.75% to 11.77 USD, 19.49% below its 20-session reference of 14.62 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The emotional hook now is loyalty: holders who sat through the slide may see 11.77 USD as the cheapest entry they will get, and every red day tests whether that conviction is a thesis or a habit.
What Is Driving It

The catalyst is the oldest trade-off in growth investing, spend now to grow later, and Reuters ties the margin hit directly to the commercial push. The market had no patience for disappointment: later the same day Roku's revenue missed on supply-chain snags and its shares fell 20%, Reuters reports [[n0949]]. The macro tape made it worse. Biden said there is a very high risk of a Russian invasion of Ukraine in the next several days [[n1532]], the US says Russia's claim of a troop withdrawal is false [[n1528]], and Al Jazeera reports US stocks took a hit as the crisis stoked fear [[n0964]]. The S&P 500 fell 2.12% to 4,380.26 index points, the Nasdaq 100 2.96% and the VIX jumped 15.73% to 28.11 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17).
The Social Signal

Palantir's drop was the sharpest on the board in a sell-off concentrated in the crowd's favourite tickers: Affirm fell 12.23%, Shopify 11.63%, SOXL 11.34%, Robinhood Markets 9.33% and ARKK 6.44% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). With the retail broker itself among the losers, the market is marking down the whole retail ecosystem at once, the platform as well as the tickers its users favour. The loudest commentary is aimed at the crowd itself: Charlie Munger says retail trading apps are creating a speculative mess, Yahoo Finance reports [[n1869]], and in Business Insider's account he blasts traders and slams crypto [[n0869]]. The faithful are being told, loudly, that they are the problem, which for a conviction crowd can harden the resolve to hold.
Historical Analog

The freshest precedent is Meta: Bloomberg reports it has lost its top-10 ranking by market value amid its worst month ever [[n0929]], and Business Insider says Tencent took a place on the list as Meta slid on the stock rout [[n0873]]. The general mechanism is simple: when a company signals that spending will rise before profits do, the market reprices the waiting period, and stocks most dependent on long-dated cash flows fall hardest. Palantir adds a crowd-specific twist. A shareholder base built on conviction tends to hold through the first drop, which can turn a one-day repricing into a slower bleed as late believers give up one by one. The pattern breaks only when the spending starts showing up as revenue the market can see.
Smart Money View

The split is stark. Cathie Wood says her innovation stocks are way undervalued and recent fund losses temporary, CNBC reports [[n1889]], buy-the-dip faith in its purest form, even as her ARKK fund fell another 6.44% to 68.18 USD on Thursday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). Munger stands at the opposite pole, treating the retail-app boom itself as the excess, and the manager of two Black Swan funds told Business Insider there are clearly heightened fears that the bubble will pop [[n1432]]. Patient money has been buying selectively rather than abandoning the crowd's platforms: Temasek added stakes in Grab, Robinhood and other consumer-focused companies, the Straits Times reports [[n1862]]. For Palantir, the debate is whether the commercial spending buys durable growth or simply dilutes margins for longer than holders can wait.
When the Narrative Breaks

The first line is the close itself: a further leg below 11.77 USD would show the margin warning is still being priced, and the 20-session reference of 14.62 USD is the level the faithful must reclaim to call this a shakeout. The macro trigger is the war. Biden's warning [[n1532]] puts weekend headlines in charge, and the Munich Security Conference, which Russia will not attend, Reuters reports [[n0119]], is the next venue for de-escalation or escalation. Rates are the quieter risk: the 10Y Treasury yield closed at 1.97% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-17), and a renewed climb would hit long-duration stories like Palantir first. A second heavy day for Robinhood, the crowd's own broker, would show the market marking down retail activity itself, not just one stock.

retail.title: Bitcoin / BTC — digital gold fails the war test
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Bitcoin's believers call it digital gold, and Thursday was the test. As shelling by Russian-backed separatists raised tensions in east Ukraine [[n1521]], gold rose 1.63% to 1,902.00 USD/oz while bitcoin fell 7.79% to 40,538.01 USD and ether 7.88% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17; Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-17). The crowd still has smart-money comfort to point to: Sequoia launched a $500 million fund to invest in crypto tokens, Forbes reports [[n1067]], and Warren Buffett invested $1 billion in a crypto-friendly bank years after calling bitcoin rat poison, Fortune notes [[n0828]].
Where It Breaks

The haven story breaks if bitcoin keeps trading like a tech stock on war days. Coinbase fell 7.71% and MicroStrategy 6.98% on the session (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), the Financial Stability Board warns of emerging risks from crypto-assets to global financial stability [[n1053]], and Yahoo Finance tells how the Big Short DAO bet against the crypto market and won [[n1063]]. A daily close below the 20-session reference of 37,784.33 USD would erase the whole rebound since late January.

retail.title: DoorDash / DASH — the pandemic habit that stuck
parts: Why Retail Is Here

If Shopify and Roblox were the pandemic trades that faded, DoorDash is the one the crowd can still believe in. The shares soared after record order numbers, CNBC reports [[n0883]]; the Japan Times headline put the surge at more than 30% [[n0884]], and the regular session closed up 10.69% at 105.03 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17). The WSJ says DoorDash showed competitors what it can eat [[n0881]], and Morningstar says the beat broke a losing streak [[n0882]]. The hook is the habit: once people order dinner from an app, they keep doing it.
Where It Breaks

DoorDash is still 17.16% below its 20-session reference of 126.78 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), so one quarter has not repaired the drawdown. Growth now depends on new categories, such as express grocery delivery with Albertsons [[n0853]], and on pricing power with restaurant partners, where DoorDash is raising fees for McDonald's outlets that keep drivers waiting, the WSJ reports [[n0472]]. If order growth slows as diners return to restaurants, the habit story becomes a reopening casualty.

retail.title: Walmart / WMT — inflation's favourite cashier
parts: Why Retail Is Here

For the crowd's defensive wing, Walmart is the inflation trade anyone can explain: when prices rise, shoppers go to the biggest discounter. Bloomberg says Walmart has a cart full of reasons to love inflation [[n0970]], Modern Retail says it is gaining grocery market share thanks to continued inflation [[n0971]], and the New York Times reports profits grew as consumers continue to spend [[n0973]]. The stock rose 4.01% to 138.88 USD on a day the S&P 500 fell 2.12% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), exactly the hiding-place behaviour a nervous crowd wants.
Where It Breaks

The same results carry the warning: Walmart says shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb, CNBC reports [[n0974]], and a consumer squeezed hard enough cuts volume, not just brands. The stock is still 1.66% below its 20-session reference of 141.22 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-17), so the bid has only begun to repair the past month's decline. If war fear fades and the crowd rushes back into growth, a defensive winner can be sold to fund it; giving back the 4.01% gain in a rebound would show it was a hiding place, not a re-rating.
